Cael Tarn.narrative: I have burned the slow pits at Sootwood for more than thirty years, and my father before me, and I do not move them for a complaint that comes up the wood road. The smoke drifts east; that is the way the wind goes and always has. I keep my axe by the door now that the wolves have come down, and I keep a tally of every load that goes out and every debt that comes in, because a burner who forgets a debt is robbed twice.
goals: keep the slow pits burning through the winter
see the east-road trade with Thistle Mossfoot stay sweet
keep Pell and Sena safe from the wolves
be paid what the quay stalls owe for charcoal
teach Pell the whole of the burn, from stacking to banking, so the pits pass to him
carve a proper tally-board for the shed so no debt can be lost or denied
Cael Tarn.mood: steady, a little grim since the wolves came down

relations.name: Sena Tarn
relations.label: partner
relations.note: She fells and trims beside me and keeps the tally straight; I would not burn without her.

relations.name: Pell Tarn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He stacks the pits well enough, but his head is full of quay boats.

relations.name: Orvin Hollis
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good woodcutter; the wolves took two of his goats and I keep my axe near for it.

relations.name: Maren Hollis
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She trades at the quay stalls and Sena thinks well of her.

relations.name: Durrow Hollis
relations.label: neighbour's boy
relations.note: Chased to his door by the wolves; a frightened lad, and no wonder.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trade
relations.note: The small-folk pedlar brings word up the east road and buys a load now and then; his complaints about smoke I hear and let pass.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Her noodle stall takes my charcoal, but she is slow to pay and quicker to talk.

relations.name: Tace Hollis
relations.label: neighbour's girl
relations.note: Orvin's daughter stacks kindling with Pell; a hard worker for her age.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: A quay builder who took offence at talk of the seawall; that is Sena's affair, not mine.

relations.name: Sena Tarn's mother
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: Never met her; she's from up the coast.

memories.gist: My father showed me how to bank a slow pit so it smoulders three days and does not flame; I have banked them the same way ever since.
Wolves took two of Orvin's goats just recently; we heard them in the night and found the blood by the plots in the morning.
A carter from Kettlebridge shorted me on a load of charcoal and laughed about it; I have not forgotten the sum or the man's face.
Pell was born in the hut between the pits in a wet autumn; Sena did not stop working until the day, and started again a week after.
The smoke from the pits has drifted east over the old forest every summer of my life; the small folk have complained before and will complain again.

stances.why: The pits are old and the wood is mine to burn; I will not move them for a complaint carried up the road.
A burner who forgets a debt is robbed twice; I keep the tally in my head and in the hut.
I have seen wolves before; when the snow comes they go back up the hills, and the axe by the door is enough until then.
Thistle Mossfoot's road brings loads and word; a soured trade costs more than a little smoke.
What Sena says to the quay builders is her business; I keep to the pits and the tally.

pastimes: sitting by the slow pits at dusk watching the smoke drift east
whittling handles and wedges from offcut wood by the door
sharing a cup at the Hollis hearth after a burn
Cael Tarn.calling: I am a charcoal burner, and I will die a charcoal burner; the slow pits are the only work I have ever wanted.

Sena Tarn.narrative: I fell and trim beside Cael and keep the tally of every load that goes down the wood road, and I have a tongue when the tally is questioned. I told the quay folk plain that the seawall will never be built and the stone price is a swindle, and I stand by it, but I do not want the wood road's loads turned back for my saying so. I have quietly offered Thistle Mossfoot a load of charcoal to smooth the smoke complaint, and I have not told Cael the whole of it.
values: a fair price for hard work
goals: keep the quay stalls buying Sootwood charcoal and baskets
mend things with Thistle Mossfoot before the east road sours
see the seawall stone come from the ridge and not from Kettlebridge
keep Pell from the forest edge until the wolves are gone
learn to write a proper letter, so the quay stalls hear from her directly and not through a carrier
see the wood road kept clear and safe enough that Pell can walk it alone
Sena Tarn.mood: brisk and a little worried about the road

relations.name: Cael Tarn
relations.label: partner
relations.note: He keeps the pits and I keep the road and the tally; between us it works.

relations.name: Pell Tarn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He says he is not afraid of the wolves, and I hear him not playing at the forest edge.

relations.name: Maren Hollis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We keep our plots side by side and trade eggs and roots; she worries about the smoke drifting east as I do.

relations.name: Orvin Hollis
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: His goats were taken and his boy chased; he has a right to be angry.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trade
relations.note: I have offered him a load of charcoal to smooth the smoke complaint; a small price for a sweet road.

relations.name: Durrow Hollis
relations.label: neighbour's boy
relations.note: A quiet lad who plays among the stacks with Pell; the wolves have shaken him.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Her stall takes our charcoal and our baskets; she counts her marks twice and pays once.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: quarrel
relations.note: He took my words about the seawall as Sootwood siding with Kettlebridge; I meant only what I said.

relations.name: Tace Hollis
relations.label: neighbour's girl
relations.note: A good worker at the pits; she and Pell are thick as thieves.

memories.gist: I told the quay builders to their faces that the seawall will never be built and the stone price is a swindle; Ostrander Vane heard it and went cold on us.
Wolves came down to the plots and took two of Orvin's goats; Durrow was chased to his door and I have kept Pell closer since.
I sold a stack of baskets at the morning stalls on the quay and came home with more marks than Cael expected; I keep half back in the hut for a lean week.
Maren Hollis and I built the goat pen together the spring before the Surge; it has stood through two hard winters.
The small folk's complaint about the smoke came up the east road with Thistle Mossfoot; I offered him a load of charcoal to smooth it and did not make a fuss about it at home.

stances.why: The ridge is ours to quarry; paying Kettlebridge's price for stone is a swindle and I say so.
The wood road carries our loads and our living; I will not have it turned back over a quarrel.
A load of charcoal to Thistle costs less than a soured east-road trade, and Cael need not be troubled with it.
The wolves have come down and taken goats; Pell stays by the stacks until they go up again.
A load unrecorded is a load unpaid; I keep the tally and I do not let it slip.

Sena Tarn.secret: I have quietly promised Thistle Mossfoot a load of charcoal to smooth the smoke complaint, and I have not told Cael the whole of it.
pastimes: walking the wood road to the Hollis door for a morning's talk
keeping the tally-book in her own hand and reading it over of an evening
tending the little herb bed behind the shed
Sena Tarn.calling: I trim and keep the tally, and I would have the loads go out fair and come back paid; that is work worth doing well.

Pell Tarn.narrative: I stack the pits with Da and carry water and kindling, and when the work is done I watch the smoke go up and think about the quay boats. I want to see the tide lanterns at Lanternquay more than anything. I say I am not afraid of the wolves, but I do not go to the forest edge any more, and at night I listen for them.
goals: see the tide lanterns at Lanternquay
crew on a quay boat one day
not let anyone see he is afraid of the wolves
see the tide lanterns at Lanternquay with his own eyes
learn to swim before he ever sets foot on a boat
Pell Tarn.mood: restless and a little frightened underneath

relations.name: Cael Tarn
relations.label: father
relations.note: Da teaches me the pits and keeps his axe by the door; he does not say much.

relations.name: Sena Tarn
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Ma keeps the tally and tells me to stay by the stacks; she worries more than she says.

relations.name: Durrow Hollis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play among the charcoal stacks; the wolves chased him to his door and he has not been the same since.

relations.name: Tace Hollis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Durrow's sister; she stacks kindling and knows a quay knot she says a boy from the harbour taught her.

relations.name: Orvin Hollis
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Durrow's da; the wolves took his goats and he is angry about it.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He tells stories of the east road and the quay.

memories.gist: Da let me bank my first slow pit by myself and it held three days; he said nothing but he nodded.
Durrow was chased to his door by the wolves and I heard him shouting; since then I stay by the stacks.
A quay man came up the wood road once and told me about the tide lanterns and the boats; I have wanted to see them ever since.

stances.why: Boats and lanterns and the harbour mouth; I will see them one day.
I say so, and I mean to make it true, but I keep by the stacks for now.

pastimes: watching the smoke rise from the pits and naming shapes in it
playing at boats with Durrow and Tace in the Hollis yard
listening to Thistle Mossfoot's tales of the quay and the pedlar roads
Pell Tarn.calling: One day I want to crew a quay boat; for now I stack the pits and carry water for Da.
